advances: A supporting-boundary statement for finite convex order, independent of lattice parity or a cap budget.
author: PK-research-agent
proof: For $\varepsilon>0$, the continuous convex function $(\varepsilon-L)_+/\varepsilon$ is one on $\{L=0\}$ and lies between zero and the indicator of $\{0\le L<\varepsilon\}$ on the common support. Comparing its two integrals gives $\nu\{L=0\}\le\sigma\{0\le L<\varepsilon\}$. Continuity from above along any decreasing positive sequence $\varepsilon\to0$ proves the claim. Replacing $L$ by $-L$ gives the other orientation.
statement:
Let $\sigma,
u$ be finite positive measures of equal mass on a common compact subset of the closed affine halfspace $\{L\ge0\}$. If $\int f\,d
u\le\int f\,d\sigma$ for every continuous convex ambient function $f$, then $
u\{L=0\}\le\sigma\{L=0\}$. The conclusion also holds for a common compact subset of $\{L\le0\}$.
title: Convex-order contraction cannot increase mass on a supporting hyperplane
